condition.label: adult degenerative scoliosis
condition.distinctions: Adult degenerative scoliosis is distinct from adult/adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; curve side alone does not establish an exercise prescription.

scope.population: Nonsurgical thoracolumbar adult degenerative scoliosis; Mixed idiopathic/degenerative scoliosis, curves 6–120 degrees; degenerative subgroup details not extracted; Adult idiopathic scoliosis, lower progression risk, main curve under 35 degrees
scope.stage: Varies by source; acute/recent versus chronic and symptom irritability are explicitly retained. Unknown stage remains unknown.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonsurgical evidence predominates; no postoperative protocol approved or inferred.
scope.exclusions: Source-specific exclusions are applicability boundaries, not diagnosis-wide contraindications. Coexisting conditions and independently selected joint limits retain precedence.
scope.uncertainty:
- No automatic scoliosis-wide ban on rotation, side bending, axial load, extension or asymmetric exercise is defensible from these retrieved studies. Likewise, no evidence-based number can be assigned to a safe load/ROM limit.
- Ordinary-training modifications must follow actual coexisting stenosis/radicular symptoms, osteoporosis/fracture risk, balance, surgery and clinician orders. Those conditions retain precedence; curve side alone cannot determine a universal “safe” side.
- Supportive exercise candidates remain research-only individualized trunk/hip strength, conditioning and balance; no execution-level therapeutic mapping approved. ADS may remain restriction-only/unresolved pending specific clinical planning rules. A primary exercise study is recorded even if no exercise is added.
- Current final ADS-specific exercise guideline not verified after targeted searches. Do not substitute adolescent idiopathic scoliosis guidelines or the adult idiopathic RCT. Long-term deformity progression, neurologic adverse outcomes and strength-training restrictions remain major gaps.

sources.design: Prospective uncontrolled cohort; 40 enrolled, 30 women completed
sources.coInterventions: Heat, TENS, ultrasound; as-needed paracetamol advised. No drug instruction transferred to app.
sources.outcomes: Bayram et al., 2024 prospective uncontrolled cohort. DOI 10.26574/maedica.2024.19.1.23, PMID 38736938, FT PMC11079735. FT. Forty nonsurgical thoracolumbar ADS participants enrolled, 30 women completed. Combined modalities (heat/TENS/ultrasound) plus stretching, strengthening, stabilization, posture/balance/coordination, 15 sessions/3 weeks, 60 min/day five days/week; home continuation. Pain/disability/QoL improved at 1/3 months. No control, ten dropouts, multiple cointerventions; no causal exercise-specific effect or long-term curve effect established. Detailed adverse-event surveillance not identified; health problems among attrition reasons cannot be assigned to treatment. Not a proof that every listed exercise is safe for all curves.

findings.statement: The uncontrolled combined-treatment cohort cannot establish bans on rotation, side bending, axial load, extension or asymmetric work, or a safe numeric load/ROM limit. Coexisting stenosis/radicular symptoms, osteoporosis, balance and surgery need their own evidence/orders. No condition-specific ordinary-training restriction is proposed from this record.

citations.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS > Conservative treatment program, journal p. 25

findings.limitations: This is a bounded evidence gap in the retrieved corpus, not proof that all training is harmless. Trial exclusions are applicability boundaries. No runtime restriction or therapeutic release follows.

gaps:
- No automatic scoliosis-wide ban on rotation, side bending, axial load, extension or asymmetric exercise is defensible from these retrieved studies. Likewise, no evidence-based number can be assigned to a safe load/ROM limit.
- Ordinary-training modifications must follow actual coexisting stenosis/radicular symptoms, osteoporosis/fracture risk, balance, surgery and clinician orders. Those conditions retain precedence; curve side alone cannot determine a universal “safe” side.
- Supportive exercise candidates remain research-only individualized trunk/hip strength, conditioning and balance; no execution-level therapeutic mapping approved. ADS may remain restriction-only/unresolved pending specific clinical planning rules. A primary exercise study is recorded even if no exercise is added.
- Current final ADS-specific exercise guideline not verified after targeted searches. Do not substitute adolescent idiopathic scoliosis guidelines or the adult idiopathic RCT. Long-term deformity progression, neurologic adverse outcomes and strength-training restrictions remain major gaps.
No exact catalog execution equivalence or numeric diagnosis-wide load/ROM/pain threshold established. All request/mapping/rule material is candidate-only, and clinical review provenance is absent.

No execution-level therapeutic mapping proposed: available direct cohort describes a combined program without exact positions; one-sided yoga case series remains partial/mixed-etiology, and adult idiopathic trial is indirect. Restriction-only/unresolved research disposition, with no invented exercise or ban.
